promise: Expose the assumptions and unanswered questions that could change a plan, then choose the next useful inquiry.
audience: People planning work in uncertain or unfamiliar territory.
trigger: Find blind spots, map uncertainty, or decide what to investigate next.

modes.name: Map
modes.when: A plan needs an uncertainty inventory.
modes.output: An evidenced four-quadrant map with priorities.

modes.name: Blindspot
modes.when: The user wants to surface unstated assumptions.
modes.output: A conversational challenge and concrete test.

modes.name: Resolve
modes.output: A selected inquiry, evidence and a reclassified map entry.

examples.title: Fictional worked example
examples.before: A migration plan treats an untested compatibility assumption as settled.
examples.after: The map records it as a consequential question with an explicit verification step.
examples.why: The next inquiry targets a decision-changing unknown.

boundaries: A brainstormed blind spot is a hypothesis; classification does not prove it exists.

verification.name: Functional acceptance
verification.expected: Supplied fictional tasks exercise actual mechanisms and failure boundaries.
verification.evidence: 31 native map/tool tests passed; installed no-engine seed/add/triage gate also passed.

verification.name: Native host acceptance
verification.expected: Actual provider/host/desktop/daemon/runner acceptance for the selected adapter.
verification.evidence: No live model, real desktop transaction, invitation, deployment or production data migration was performed by this functional baseline.

sources.role: Primary retained owner history, mechanisms and records; portable method consolidates the listed entry points.

consolidation: One portable method entry with mode references; original native engines, agents and records retained as optional adapters.
